comment: src/Microcosm.cpp at commit b90cd69. The twenty-five cells share one line each for their button, their jack and their output, since they differ only in which cell they belong to; the maker names them A1 to E5, lettered across and numbered down. The stored pattern on a new module is set in initSaved() at line 89 to cells 11, 12, 13, 16 and 22, which is a glider. Every trigger is formed as SchmittTrigger.process(jack voltage + button value), so a held button pins the trigger high and a jack cannot fire while it is held. The generation is computed from a copy of the grid taken at the top of process(), so all cells change together, but a cell button or jack fired on the same sample as a clock is applied to the live grid first and then overwritten by the rule. The clock switch gates the step only; the save, restore, random and clear jacks work whatever it is set to. Randomize uses std::rand rather than Rack's own generator.
